transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Fiona. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Fiona. I built a timber garden office sixty feet away from the main house, but the Wi-Fi signal from our Hub 5 cannot penetrate the exterior double-glazed patio doors and foil-backed wall insulation!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how frustrating poor wireless coverage is when you are trying to work productively from an external garden workspace. Let's explore your network expansion options immediately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Fiona. I am an independent architectural consultant and I rely completely on stable high-speed cloud synchronization to upload multi-gigabyte Revit 3D building models for commercial contractors.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What physical wiring or cabling currently exists between the main house and your garden building?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I hired an electrician who ran a forty-meter exterior-grade Cat6 copper Ethernet cable through an underground PVC conduit into Port 2 on the back of the Hub 5 in the hallway.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check the port status and local Ethernet interface telemetry on your broadband hub.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: When I plug my work laptop directly into that wall socket in the garden office, I get nine hundred megabits with zero latency.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is that Cat6 link terminating into a wall faceplate with an RJ45 modular socket, or does it connect directly into a secondary network switch?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It terminates into a shielded metal faceplate on the timber wall with two RJ45 jacks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have you attempted connecting a secondary wireless access point or router to that faceplate?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I bought a cheap third-party Wi-Fi extender off Amazon, but it created a separate network SSID and keeps causing IP address conflicts with the main router.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Third-party consumer extenders configured with active DHCP servers generate double-NAT conflicts and routing loop errors.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Every time my tablet roams between the main house and the garden office, the internet completely freezes for two minutes!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When devices move between mismatched wireless subnets without 802.11k and 802.11v seamless roaming protocols, the TCP connection drops.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there an official S-Net mesh hardware solution that integrates seamlessly with our Hub 5?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, we provide S-Net Intelligent Wi-Fi Booster pods that support wired Ethernet backhaul mode.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How does wired Ethernet backhaul work with the Booster pods?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In wired backhaul mode, the booster pod connects directly to your Cat6 wall socket, using the physical gigabit copper link as its high-speed backbone instead of relaying over an attenuated wireless mesh signal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That sounds ideal because the copper cable eliminates all wireless wall attenuation.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me on hold for about forty seconds while I query your Hub 5 port configuration to verify Gigabit auto-negotiation on Port 2.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience while holding. The Port 2 hardware status indicates full-duplex one thousand megabits auto-negotiation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That confirms the electrician terminated all eight copper wires properly without any crossed pairs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, all four twisted pairs are transmitting at gigabit carrier frequencies.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the S-Net Booster pod broadcast the exact same Wi-Fi network name and password as the main Hub?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The booster clones your existing SSID and WPA3 security key, forming a single unified mesh network across your entire property.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So my phone and laptop will roam seamlessly without dropping video calls when I walk out to the garden?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our automated client-steering software will dynamically shift your connection between the house and garden pod within five milliseconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How much does the S-Net Wi-Fi Booster pod cost per month?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under your Gigafast 900 package tier, you are entitled to up to three Wi-Fi Booster pods free of charge under our Whole Home Wi-Fi Guarantee.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Free of charge is fantastic! I was expecting to pay a monthly hardware rental fee.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will dispatch a complimentary Wi-Fi Booster pod via express courier today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: When can I expect the parcel to arrive at our house?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The unit will be delivered by DPD tracked courier tomorrow afternoon before three o'clock.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will I need to configure any complex IP settings on my computer to set it up?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Setup is entirely plug-and-play: connect the included Ethernet patch lead from the wall faceplate into the booster's LAN port and plug in the power supply.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the booster configure its operating mode automatically?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The internal firmware automatically detects the gigabit Ethernet link and switches from wireless repeater mode to wired access point mode within sixty seconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That makes setup completely foolproof.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You should also power down and remove that third-party Amazon extender to eliminate radio frequency co-channel interference.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will unplug the Amazon extender and toss it in the recycling bin.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The booster broadcasts dual-band Wi-Fi 6 on both the 2.4GHz and 5GHz radio bands with sixteen hundred megabits aggregate wireless throughput.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will easily deliver four to five hundred megabits wirelessly throughout the garden office.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Even on heavy architectural 3D rendering file syncs, you will experience zero wireless bottlenecks.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I was in the middle of uploading a four-gigabyte architectural file to the client cloud drive yesterday when the old extender crashed and corrupted the entire model! I had to spend three hours rebuilding the drawings from scratch!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how intensely frustrating that is, especially having to rebuild three hours of complex 3D CAD modeling work. The wired Ethernet backhaul pod will provide the rock-solid stability you need.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, that reassurance really helps my peace of mind for future client deadlines.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you remind me how long that outdoor Ethernet cable is and whether it is running through a protective conduit?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: As I explained earlier, the outdoor Cat6 cable is forty meters long and runs through an underground PVC conduit.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for confirming that specification. Forty meters is well within the one-hundred-meter maximum distance for copper gigabit Ethernet.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That confirms signal degradation won't be an issue over forty meters.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our hardware telemetry verifies zero packet attenuation across the four-pair run.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And does the booster have extra Ethernet ports for connecting a wired printer?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the booster unit features two Gigabit Ethernet ports on the base, allowing you to daisy-chain a desktop PC or network printer.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is extremely convenient so I don't need to install an extra switch.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: How is your broadband connection performing otherwise inside the main residential house?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Inside the main house the Wi-Fi is blazing fast, we get over eight hundred megabits in the living room and kitchen, so the fiber service itself has been outstanding.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am delighted to hear the gigabit optical connection performs so reliably throughout the main residence.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It was purely extending it out to the garden office that was giving me a headache.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The hardware dispatch order reference number is POD-99412-W.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Noted down... POD-99412-W.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have verified that the complimentary Wi-Fi Booster pod is dispatched via DPD for tomorrow afternoon delivery, your port configuration is verified at full gigabit speed, and your Whole Home Wi-Fi guarantee is permanently applied. Does that completely resolve your inquiry today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes Fiona, you've provided the exact solution I needed and answered every technical question. Thank you very much.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today. Have a productive afternoon in your garden studio. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Fiona, goodbye.
